```{r}
# ======================================================================
# CONTINUATION OF REFERENCE CODE
# Problem: Role of qualitative (ordinal) predictors in multiple linear regression
# ======================================================================

# Load required libraries
library(ggplot2)
library(stargazer)
library(dplyr)

# The data is already loaded from the reference code
# df1 and df2 are already created
# Let's ensure we have a clean dataset to work with

data(diamonds)
df <- as.data.frame(diamonds)

# Identify ordinal categorical variables and response
cat("========================================\n")
cat("ORDINAL CATEGORICAL VARIABLES IN DIAMONDS DATASET:\n")
cat("========================================\n")
cat("1. cut: Fair < Good < Very Good < Premium < Ideal\n")
cat("2. color: D (best) < E < F < G < H < I < J (worst)\n")
cat("3. clarity: I1 < SI2 < SI1 < VS2 < VS1 < VVS2 < VVS1 < IF\n")
cat("\nResponse variable: price (in US dollars)\n")
cat("========================================\n\n")

# ======================================================================
# (a) Run a linear regression of the response on the quality of cut
# ======================================================================

cat("PART (a): Linear regression of price on cut quality\n")
cat("----------------------------------------------------\n")

# Using the approach from reference code with releveling
df_cut <- df
df_cut$cut <- factor(df_cut$cut, ordered = FALSE)
# Relevel to have "Ideal" as reference for easier interpretation
df_cut$cut <- relevel(df_cut$cut, ref = "Ideal")

model_cut <- lm(price ~ cut, data = df_cut)
cat("Fitted Regression Model:\n")
cat("price = ", round(coef(model_cut)[1], 2))
for(i in 2:length(coef(model_cut))) {
  cat(" + ", round(coef(model_cut)[i], 2), "*cut", names(coef(model_cut))[i], sep="")
}
cat("\n\n")
summary(model_cut)
stargazer(model_cut, type = "text", title = "Model: Price ~ Cut")

# Alternative using as.character to avoid default ordering (as in reference)
model_test <- lm(price ~ relevel(factor(as.character(cut)), ref="Ideal"), data=diamonds)
cat("\nAlternative model (using as.character):\n")
summary(model_test)
```


```{r}
# ======================================================================
# (b) Test whether expected price of diamond with premium cut is 
#     significantly different from that of the ideal cut
# ======================================================================

cat("\n\nPART (b): Testing Premium Cut vs Ideal Cut\n")
cat("-------------------------------------------\n")

# From model_cut, the coefficient for cutPremium directly tests this
premium_coef <- summary(model_cut)$coefficients["cutPremium", ]
cat("Coefficient for cutPremium:", round(premium_coef["Estimate"], 2), "\n")
cat("Standard Error:", round(premium_coef["Std. Error"], 2), "\n")
cat("t-value:", round(premium_coef["t value"], 2), "\n")
cat("p-value:", format.pval(premium_coef["Pr(>|t|)"], digits=4), "\n")

if(premium_coef["Pr(>|t|)"] < 0.05) {
  cat("\nCONCLUSION: The expected price of diamond with PREMIUM cut is")
  cat(" SIGNIFICANTLY DIFFERENT from IDEAL cut (p < 0.05).\n")
} else {
  cat("\nCONCLUSION: The expected price of diamond with PREMIUM cut is")
  cat(" NOT significantly different from IDEAL cut.\n")
}

# Verify with actual means (as in reference code)
cat("\nVerification using actual means:\n")
cut_means <- aggregate(df$price, by=list(cut=df$cut), mean)
print(cut_means)

premium_actual <- cut_means$x[cut_means$cut == "Premium"]
ideal_actual <- cut_means$x[cut_means$cut == "Ideal"]
cat("\nActual mean difference (Premium - Ideal): $", 
    round(premium_actual - ideal_actual, 2), "\n")
```


```{r}
# ======================================================================
# (c) What is the expected price of a diamond of ideal cut?
# ======================================================================

cat("\n\nPART (c): Expected Price for Ideal Cut\n")
cat("----------------------------------------\n")

# From model_cut with Ideal as reference, the intercept is the expected price
ideal_price <- coef(model_cut)["(Intercept)"]
cat("From regression model: $", round(ideal_price, 2), "\n")

# Using predict function
new_ideal <- data.frame(cut = factor("Ideal", levels = levels(df_cut$cut)))
pred_ideal <- predict(model_cut, newdata = new_ideal)
cat("Using predict(): $", round(pred_ideal, 2), "\n")

# Actual mean
actual_ideal <- mean(df$price[df$cut == "Ideal"])
cat("Actual mean price for Ideal cut: $", round(actual_ideal, 2), "\n")

# Using the aggregate result from above
cat("From aggregate: $", round(ideal_actual, 2), "\n")
```

```{r}
# ======================================================================
# (d) Modify the regression model by incorporating the predictor "table"
# ======================================================================

cat("\n\nPART (d): Model with Cut + Table\n")
cat("----------------------------------\n")

model_table <- lm(price ~ cut + table, data = df_cut)
cat("Fitted Regression Model:\n")
cat("price = ", round(coef(model_table)[1], 2))
cat(" + ", round(coef(model_table)["table"], 2), "*table")
for(i in 2:5) {
  cat(" + ", round(coef(model_table)[i], 2), "*cut", names(coef(model_table))[i], sep="")
}
cat("\n\n")
summary(model_table)
stargazer(model_table, type = "text", title = "Model: Price ~ Cut + Table")
```

```{r}
# ======================================================================
# (e) Test for the significance of "table" in predicting price
# ======================================================================

cat("\n\nPART (e): Testing Significance of Table\n")
cat("----------------------------------------\n")

table_coef <- summary(model_table)$coefficients["table", ]
cat("Coefficient for table:", round(table_coef["Estimate"], 4), "\n")
cat("Standard Error:", round(table_coef["Std. Error"], 4), "\n")
cat("t-value:", round(table_coef["t value"], 2), "\n")
cat("p-value:", format.pval(table_coef["Pr(>|t|)"], digits=4), "\n")

# F-test comparing models with and without table
anova_result <- anova(model_cut, model_table)
cat("\nANOVA comparison (Model without table vs with table):\n")
print(anova_result)

if(table_coef["Pr(>|t|)"] < 0.05) {
  cat("\nCONCLUSION: Table is a SIGNIFICANT predictor of diamond price (p < 0.05).\n")
} else {
  cat("\nCONCLUSION: Table is NOT a significant predictor of diamond price.\n")
}
```

```{r}
# ======================================================================
# (f) Find the average estimated price of a diamond with an average 
#     table value and which is of fair cut
# ======================================================================

cat("\n\nPART (f): Average Estimated Price (Fair Cut, Average Table)\n")
cat("------------------------------------------------------------\n")

# Calculate average table value
avg_table <- mean(df$table, na.rm = TRUE)
cat("Average table value:", round(avg_table, 2), "\n")

# Create new data point for Fair cut with average table
new_fair <- data.frame(
  cut = factor("Fair", levels = levels(df_cut$cut)),
  table = avg_table
)

# Predict price with confidence interval
pred_fair <- predict(model_table, newdata = new_fair, interval = "confidence")

cat("\nFor a diamond with:\n")
cat("- Cut: FAIR\n")
cat("- Table value:", round(avg_table, 2), "(average)\n")
cat("\nAverage estimated price: $", round(pred_fair[1], 2), "\n")
cat("95% Confidence Interval: [$", round(pred_fair[2], 2), ", $", round(pred_fair[3], 2), "]\n")

# For comparison, also calculate for other cuts with average table
cat("\nFor comparison (all cuts with average table):\n")
cut_levels <- levels(df_cut$cut)
for(cut_type in cut_levels) {
  new_data <- data.frame(
    cut = factor(cut_type, levels = levels(df_cut$cut)),
    table = avg_table
  )
  pred <- predict(model_table, newdata = new_data)
  cat("  ", cut_type, ": $", round(pred, 2), "\n")
}
```
